items.text: Blepharoplasty procedure and/or a repair for blepharoptosis is reimbursable when it is considered medically necessary.
items.rationale: The coverage verb - reimbursable when medically necessary. Drives both certify.Met leaves.

items.text: The service is considered medically necessary when performed as functional/reconstructive surgery to correct one of the following:
items.rationale: Defines medical necessity as ONE requirement: the surgery is performed as functional/reconstructive surgery TO CORRECT one of four listed indications. This is encoded as a SINGLE CODED QUESTION - "Which Listed Indication Is This Functional Or Reconstructive Surgery Performed To Correct" - whose nine options are the four bullets, bullet 1 held at its six-way etiology x finding decomposition. THIS REVERSES AN EARLIER RULING RECORDED HERE, and the history matters. A first pass argued the four indications operationalize "functional/reconstructive" so no positive purpose leaf was needed. A KE-judge caught that as too broad - having an indication and operating to correct it ARE different facts - and the fix was one PURPOSE atom per source item conjoined with that item in its own OR-arm. That fix was right about the gap and wrong about the remedy: it created two sides that could DISAGREE. Nothing stopped a submitter asserting "Patient Has Prosthesis Difficulties" together with "Requested To Correct The Symptomatic Redundant Skin", because those atoms sat in different arms and the tree accepted the mismatch. The fusion closes the same gap STRUCTURALLY instead of by conjunction: one answer names what the surgery corrects, and one answer cannot contradict itself. It also stops a hollowing the judge flagged separately - the four purpose concepts were named "Requested As FUNCTIONAL OR RECONSTRUCTIVE Surgery To Correct ..." while their codes read `requested-to-correct-...`, so the code, which is the assertion identity, silently dropped the qualifier and was broader than its own label. The qualifier now sits in the QUESTION text where it governs all nine options at once and cannot be dropped from one. COST, stated: seven CEL cases retired (four PURPOSE and three INDICATION discriminators). They are not merely deleted - the state they probed no longer exists to test. The residual "the surgery corrects something the policy does not list" case survives as the `none of the listed indications` answer, which is also the one-answer denial for this whole criterion.

items.text: Impairment of near or far vision or visual field defect due to dermatochalasis, blepharochalasis or blepharoptosis
items.rationale: Indication 1, now SIX OPTIONS of the fused question rather than six leaves: three etiologies x two finding types. The etiologies were always split. The FINDING AXIS was not, and that was under-depth: vision impairment and a visual field defect are separately measured (acuity vs perimetry) and the policy own evidence layer keeps them apart, requiring "either a photograph or the visual field examination printout". "near or far" RIDES - nothing branches on which. The causal "due to" rides IN each leaf: modelling findings and etiologies as separate concepts joined by AND would let an unpaired combination qualify, dropping the causal attribution.

items.text: Symptomatic redundant skin weighing down or upper lashes
items.rationale: Indication 2, one option of the fused question. SOURCE DEFECT: reads "weighing down or upper lashes". RESOLVED by the customer on review flag c7dd860f, which supplies the intended wording "Symptomatic redundant skin weighing down upper lashes" - the concept carries that wording verbatim, not a KE repair. "Symptomatic" is load-bearing and rides in the identity.

items.text: Chronic, symptomatic dermatitis of pretarsal skin caused by redundant upper lid skin
items.rationale: Indication 3, one option of the fused question. All three qualifiers ride in the identity: chronicity, symptoms, and the causal attribution to redundant lid skin.

items.text: Prosthesis difficulties in an anophthalmic socket
items.rationale: Indication 4, one option of the fused question. All but unreachable in practice - the complaint list offers nothing an anophthalmic-socket patient necessarily reports. Encoded as written and pinned by a CEL case.

items.text: A blepharoplasty procedure and/or a repair for blepharoptosis is not a benefit when performed for cosmetic purposes.
items.rationale: The benefit exclusion, its OWN branch evaluated first. Not the complement of the indication set: a request can fail every indication without being cosmetic, and a cosmetic request can carry documentation that satisfies an indication. Reported as not-certify.Unmet - the source states a REASON, not a second disposition.

items.text: A Treatment Authorization Request (TAR) is required for a blepharoplasty procedure and/or a repair for blepharoptosis.
items.rationale: TAR submission is an upstream workflow requirement; the decision evaluates the medical policy criteria for the requested procedures.

items.text: When requesting a TAR or a Service Authorization Request (SAR), providers must include documentation of the patient complaints and either a photograph or the visual field examination printout.
items.rationale: The TAR documentation requirement: complaints AND (photograph OR visual-field printout). Supplies the conjunctive structure of the Met guard. It never requires the evidence to MATCH the claimed indication - each list quantifies independently.

items.text: Patient complaints must include one or more of the following:
items.rationale: Opens the complaint disjunction. ONE CODED QUESTION with seven options (kit inline-answer-options, CRL #189), read by the "Qualifying Patient Complaint Documented" criterion. THIS REVERSES AN EARLIER RULING RECORDED HERE, and the earlier reasoning is worth stating because it was half right. It argued for independent booleans on two grounds: that "one or more of the following" means complaints co-occur, and that an unanswered question must read as an unmet complaint rather than pausing the tree. The SECOND ground was simply wrong on its own terms - a bare code-is boolean is VALUE-READ, so an unanswered one is UNKNOWN and DOES pause. Independent booleans never delivered the property they were chosen for; the coded question does, through its mandatory "none of the listed complaints" option, which reaches a determinate false in ONE answer where seven booleans needed seven. The FIRST ground is true and is the real cost: complaints genuinely can co-occur, and a coded question has ONE answer slot arbitrated by most recent this, so only one qualifying complaint can ever be recorded. That is acceptable here ONLY because the criterion is a pure disjunction and the source requirement is satisfied by one member - "must include one or more" is met by one, and nothing downstream counts them. If anything ever needs the full set, this is the decision to revisit.

items.text: Interference with near or distance vision or visual field;
items.rationale: Complaint bullet 1, TWO leaves. Same structure as indication 1: "near or distance" qualifies vision and rides; vision vs visual FIELD are separately measured and split.

items.text: Difficulty seeing at distance and/or near due to upper eyelid drooping, looking through the eyelashes or seeing the upper eyelid skin; or
items.rationale: Complaint bullet 2, THREE leaves - upper eyelid drooping, looking through the eyelashes, and seeing the upper eyelid skin are three mechanisms a patient reports separately. "at distance and/or near" qualifies the verb and rides. Leaving this fused while the SIBLING bullet was split on identical reasoning was a half-split, not an adjudicated choice.

items.text: Chronic blepharitis or dermatitis
items.rationale: Complaint options 3 and 4 - TWO distinct diagnoses a chart records separately, so two options rather than one -or- answer.

items.text: Photographs must demonstrate one or more of the following:
items.rationale: Opens the photograph demonstrations. The criterion "Qualifying Objective Demonstration Submitted" is now TWO EVIDENCE LANES, each a conformance atom conjoined with that lane's coded question: four photographic options, two visual-field options. A packet may still carry a photograph AND a visual field, because those are two DIFFERENT questions and therefore two independent answer slots. CONFORMANCE NO LONGER RIDES IN THE LEAF IDENTITY. Every leaf used to begin "Conforming ...", which asked the same submission-standards question six times and made one true state inexpressible: a photograph that SHOWS the finding but does NOT meet the page-3 standards. The source states those standards ONCE PER LANE and they govern the SUBMISSION, not each finding, so they are now one atomic question per lane - separately answerable and separately deniable, with three CEL cases pinning that they can deny.

items.text: The upper eyelid margin approaches to within 2.5 mm (1/4 of the diameter of the visible iris) of the corneal light reflex.
items.rationale: Demonstration option 1. POLARITY: "to within 2.5 mm" means 2.5 mm OR LESS - a smaller margin-to-reflex distance is worse ptosis and is what qualifies. Named in the source direction so it cannot be inverted to "at least". GLOSS, NOT AN ALTERNATIVE: an earlier name read "Within 2.5 Mm OR One Quarter Iris Diameter", which made either independently sufficient and was BROADER than the sentence. The parenthetical explains the 2.5 mm, so the name now reads "Equivalent To". Concept names are the question text a clinician reads, so an overstated name becomes an overstated question.

items.text: The upper eyelid skin rests on the eyelashes.
items.rationale: Demonstration option 2.

items.text: The upper eyelid indicates the presence of dermatitis.
items.rationale: Demonstration option 3.

items.text: The upper eyelid position contributes to difficulty tolerating a prosthesis in an anophthalmic socket.
items.rationale: Demonstration option 4.

items.text: Visual field examination must demonstrate a minimum of 12 degree or 30 percent loss of upper field of vision with upper lid skin and/or lid margin in respose and elevated (by taping the lid) to demonstrate potential correction by the proposed procedure or procedures.
items.rationale: Demonstration options 5 and 6, now the two options of the "Visual Field Demonstration Submitted" coded question - two DIFFERENT measured quantities (angular degrees, percentage of field), either of which satisfies. The repose-and-elevated comparison rides in both: it is the attributability requirement (the loss must be correctable by the proposed surgery), not a camera setting. "respose" is a source typo for "repose", corrected in the option identity. The examination-method standards (Goldmann III 4-E or equivalent automated perimeter, 10dB stimulus, 50-60 degrees above fixation, the tangent-screen alternative) are carried by the lane's own conformance atom rather than by these option names.

items.text:
Providers must conform to the following standards when submitting photographs:
Prints not slides must be frontal, canthus-to-canthus with the head perpendicular to the plane of the camera (not tilted) to demonstrate a skin rash or position of the true lid margin or the pseudo-lid margin.
The photos must be of sufficient clarity to show a light reflex on the cornea.If redundant skin coexists with true lid ptosis, additional photos must be taken with the upper lid skin retracted to show the actual position of the true lid margin (needed if both CPT code 15822 and 15823 are required and planned in addition to codes 67901 thru 67908).
Oblique photos are only needed to demonstrate redundant skin on the upper eyelashes when this is the only indication for surgery.
items.rationale: THE PHOTOGRAPH SUBMISSION STANDARDS, encoded as ONE conformance criterion covering the WHOLE section. "Providers MUST conform" is mandatory language constraining what counts as valid evidence, so a non-conforming submission is not evidence at all. The concept is "Submitted Photographs Conform To The Photograph Submission Standards", conjoined with the photographic demonstration question in that evidence lane and pinned by demonstration-photograph-non-conforming-unmet, which proves a submission that SHOWS a listed finding but does not meet the standards is denied. THIS ITEM CITES TWO SPANS, and the second one is a CORRECTION. The unconditional standards (frontal canthus-to-canthus prints not slides, head perpendicular, clarity sufficient to show the corneal light reflex) and the TWO CONDITIONAL bullets are all part of the same "following standards", so the conformance question covers all of them. An earlier pass cited only the opening mandate and left the conditional bullets in ignoredRanges with a rationale saying they were subsumed elsewhere or were mere relaxations. That was INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: a concept named "... Conform To The Photograph Submission Standards" claims the whole section, so filing part of that section as non-criterion narrative asserts both that it is covered and that it is not. A KE-judge arm caught the contradiction. The spans are now CITED. WHAT THE CONDITIONAL BULLETS MEAN INSIDE THIS ONE QUESTION, since they do not each become a leaf: a submitter attesting conformance is attesting to the standards AS APPLICABLE TO THEIR SUBMISSION. (a) "If redundant skin coexists with true lid ptosis, additional photos must be taken with the upper lid skin retracted" applies when that coexistence holds - and the requirement it serves, "both must be individually documented", ALSO has its own two per-procedure leaves, so the photograph is the evidentiary mechanism while the leaves are the criterion. (b) "Oblique photos are ONLY NEEDED ... when this is the ONLY indication for surgery" is a relaxation OUTSIDE its condition and a positive requirement INSIDE it; both directions are held by one attestation, where a standalone required leaf would ADD a burden the source removes in the ordinary case. THE GRAIN IS THE HONEST ONE: no engine at this stage can check whether an oblique photograph was included or whether the lid skin was retracted. The assertable unit is the attestation by the submitter that the submission meets the standards, and splitting it into per-bullet leaves would manufacture questions nobody can answer from the artifact a reviewer holds.

items.text: Providers must conform to the following standards when submitting visual field examination printout:
items.rationale: THE VISUAL FIELD EXAMINATION STANDARDS, the second evidence lane's equivalent, and encoded on the same reasoning: "Providers must conform" is mandatory and a non-conforming examination is not evidence. One atomic question - "Submitted Visual Field Examination Conforms To The Visual Field Examination Standards" - conjoined with the visual-field demonstration question, pinned by demonstration-visual-field-non-conforming-unmet. The METHOD detail (Goldmann Perimeter III 4-E or an equivalent programmable automated perimeter, 10dB stimulus, 50-60 degrees above fixation, 4-degree vertical separation from 24 degrees, no wider than 10-degree horizontal separation, the at-rest-and-elevated repeat, and the 1-metre tangent-screen alternative with a 2-5 mm white test object) RIDES in this one conformance question rather than becoming a leaf per instrument setting. That is the right grain: a submitter attests that the examination was performed to the stated standard, and no engine at this stage can check a perimeter configuration. The at-rest-and-elevated requirement additionally rides in the two demonstration option identities, because there it is the attributability claim (the loss must be surgically correctable), not an instrument setting.

items.text: If both a blepharoplasty and a ptosis repair are planned, both must be individually documented.
items.rationale: Applies ONLY on the both-requested branch, as TWO per-procedure leaves conjoined in the guard - the source says each must be individually documented, so a reviewer can see WHICH one is missing. The source does not say what happens when only one of the two is documented (deny the pair, or certify the documented one); this stage emits one determination per run so partial certification is inexpressible, encoded as deny-the-pair and flagged.
